rui: heads-up: ran probe-warmup sampler across hosted/dedicated/private. quick summary in thread. TL;DR: hosted hit-rate +15% vs private. need help interpreting.
ashley: numbers?
rui: hosted: 0.88 hit@prefix, dedicated: 0.79, private: 0.69. baseline (no sampler): ~0.62 across all. sample config used:
```
sample_rate=0.03
probe_fraction=0.2
prefill_async=true
key_normalize=true
ttl=300
```
kevin: interesting — private worst. what's storage backend for private tests?
rui: private used customer NFS via VPC (long tail 30-120ms for small files). dedicated used local NVMe-backed netstore (10-20ms). hosted uses intra-region object cache + memstore warmup.
priya: so latency -> miss amplification? Were there evictions during warmup?
rui: yes. observed 4x higher eviction churn on private nodes. profiler shows many short-lived KV entries — likely due to async prefill timing + slower write ack. snippet:
```
[2026-02-12 09:12:03] kv_put key=prefix:abc latency=78ms prefill_retries=2 evicted=true
[2026-02-12 09:12:03] prefill_worker id=3 queued=12 processing=3
```
mike: kernel selection differences? could different sequence len perf change batching -> affect warmup rate?
rui: good call. On private we picked CPU fallback kernels for some tensor ops (driver mismatch in private image). That slowed batch throughput and delayed prefill pipeline. kernel log: `kernel_selector: fallback_cpu=true`
ashley: @kevin @priya proposals: 1) disable async prefill for VPC-backed netstores, use synchronous verified writes; 2) increase probe_fraction to 0.4 for private for a short warmup window; 3) add retry amplification limiter to prevent eviction storms.
kevin: agree. also add short-term TTL bump (600s) for prefills during deployment window. ops-bot can you schedule a canary run?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job scheduled on dedicated/hosted (10% traffic) at 1942001280. Notifying infra on VPC patch window.
priya: if we do TTL bump, ensure we annotate prefill entries with `prefill=true` so cleanup later doesn't affect real traffic analytics.
rui: noted. I'll open a tiny PR with config changes + measurement dashboard. baseline + sampler diffs attached after canary. thanks :thumbsup:
